A single `grep -rin repair` over the Android scripts dir surfaces it in the first 20 hits. This should have been HELD, not STILL_UNHELD.

The 14 HEX_ role constants (WarHex.as:11-37) and the narrow/sarrow/earrow/warrow children (:41,:43,:47,:55) are verbatim — QUOTE_UNVERIFIED overturned. But the headline geometry is false: the board is a 6x6 SQUARE lattice with no odd-row offset — WarHexUI.as:350 `for(i = 0; i < 6; i++)` / :352 `for(j = 0; j < 6; j++)` / :359 `hex.x = 90 + xpos * 55;` / :360 `hex.y = 92 + ypos * 55;` — and adjacency is strictly cardinal 4-way (getExitOwner, :443-464, branches only on xpos==0/5 and ypos==0/5; WarHex.as:219-222 gates the same four arrows). A hex grid needs a per-row x offset and six neighbours; neither exists. The cells are DRAWN as hexagons ([Embed] symbol622) but the topology is square, so 'not a square grid' is exactly backwards.

The refutation is sound and I re-derived it. §1t99s0§.as:3094 Light = base * 1.4 with NO mastery term at all; :3105 Balanced = base * (1 + 0.2*m*0.1), i.e. >= 1.0x base at m=0 and 1.2x at m=10. new_findings.text: A seventh combat-tuning divergence the build-divergence claim missed: the SPEED-to-skill-cooldown clamp is 300 in Android v0.682 but 600 in web v0.717. Both give a 50% maximum cooldown reduction and both apply the SPEED buff x1.5 before the clamp, so only the cap constant moved — but it halves the effective value of SPEED for cooldowns in the build this project targets.
new_findings.ledger_text: SPEED 300 is the cooldown cap
new_findings.lane_impact: L-skills-meters / L-progression: any SPEED-scaling CONTRACT must be tagged per build; add this row to the build-divergence table before any of it is marked CONTRACT.

new_findings.text: The War-Room board is a 6x6 SQUARE lattice, not a hex grid: cells are laid out on a uniform 55 px pitch with no odd-row offset and adjacency is strictly 4-way cardinal (N/S/E/W), with the four board edges (xpos or ypos == 0 or 5) exiting to the neighbouring territory. The cells are drawn as hexagon art (class WarHex, [Embed] symbol622) which is what makes the name misleading.
new_findings.ledger_text: War board is a hexagonal grid
new_findings.lane_impact: L-meta-social: prevents an implementer building cube/axial hex coordinates for what is a 6x6 square board; the 14 typed cell roles and the arrow rendering survive unchanged.

new_findings.text: Reach IS per-stance in the engine, closing the ledger blocker the packet's own claim #0 said was still open. MCSPlayer.setStance converts baseSlashLength (StatsManager.getBaseSlashLengthVal = 120 + floor((90 + DAN*5) * speed / (20 + speed))) into the live reach: LIGHT x1.5, BALANCED x(1 + 0.5*balancedMastery*0.01), HEAVY x(0.5 + 0.5*heavyMastery*0.01) floored at 100, REVERSED x1.5, DUAL x1 floored at 100 — then pushes it to InputManager.setMaxDistance. Note LIGHT carries no mastery term at all; lightMastery is spent on damage instead (MCSPlayer.as:3205).
new_findings.quote: case LIGHT_STANCE: this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * 1.5; ... case BALANCED_STANCE: this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * (1 + 0.5 * this.balancedMastery * 0.01); ... case HEAVY_STANCE: this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * (0.5 + 0.5 * this.heavyMastery * 0.01); if(this.slashLength < 100) { this.slashLength = 100; } ... case REVERSED_STANCE: this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * 1.5; ... case DUAL_STANCE: this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength; if(this.slashLength < 100) { this.slashLength = 100; } ... InputManager.setMaxDistance(this.slashLength);
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 COMBAT CORE / L-art-anim-feel: the ledger's 'reach cap in px per stance' blocker is CLOSED. Reach = getBaseSlashLengthVal(speed) x the stance factor above, in an 800-px-wide game stage (StatsManager.as:80), i.e. 2.4 screen px per game px in a 1080p capture.
new_findings.ledger_text: Combat numbers: reach cap in px per stance.

new_findings.text: The reload/Focus bar's maximum is a flat constant, not 48 + SPEED*6, and the two builds use DIFFERENT constants. StatsManager.getBaseReload() (48 + SPEED*6) is computed, passed into MCSPlayer.initPlayer and stored at :190 — and then never read anywhere in the bundle. :239 unconditionally sets maxreload = 5*24 = 120 (EnemyClone.as:77 does the same). The web v0.717 build sets 8*24 = 192. A recreation that scales the meter with SPEED is modelling something the original does not do.
new_findings.quote: MCSPlayer.as:190 'this.baseReload = baseReload;' — grep across the bundle finds declaration (:105), parameter (:182) and this assignment, and NO read. MCSPlayer.as:239 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;'. §1t99s0§.as:249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;'.
new_findings.build: both — 120 on android v0.682, 192 on web v0.717
new_findings.lane_impact: L-skills-meters / L-combat-core / L-ui-hud: the Focus/reload max is a CONTRACT constant of 192 for the web v0.717 target. 48 + SPEED*6 must not be implemented.

new_findings.text: A full reload bar IS the crit condition, and stance mastery scales damage — neither is mentioned anywhere in the packet, which treats the bar purely as a slash budget. getDamage rolls baseDamage = minDamage + random()*damageRange, applies a stance factor (LIGHT x(0.5 + 0.5*lightMastery*0.01), BALANCED x(1 + 0.5*balancedMastery*0.01), HEAVY/DUAL/REVERSED x1.5), and then, only when reload == maxreload, returns maxDamage*1.2 + STAT_CRITICALDMG (x1.5 in LIGHT).
new_findings.quote: internal function getDamage() : int { var baseDamage:int = this.minDamage + Math.random() * this.damageRange; switch(this.stance) { case LIGHT_STANCE: maxDamage = baseDamage * (0.5 + 0.5 * this.lightMastery * 0.01); ... case HEAVY_STANCE: case DUAL_STANCE: case REVERSED_STANCE: maxDamage = baseDamage * 1.5; } if(this.reload == this.maxreload) { if(this.stance != LIGHT_STANCE) { return maxDamage * 1.2 + this.STAT_CRITICALDMG; } return maxDamage * 1.5 + this.STAT_CRITICALDMG; } return maxDamage; }
new_findings.lane_impact: L-combat-core / L-skills-meters: this is the mechanism behind 'OG has NO Critical meter (Focus buys evasion)' in the session-11 memory — the crit is bought by a FULL reload bar, and the stance mastery stats are damage multipliers, not cosmetic ranks.

new_findings.text: A third shipped data bug the packet misses: itemdata.xml contains a completely EMPTY item record — item 7075 has an <id> and nothing else. It parses to type 0 = ARMOR, displayname "", gvalue 1, art 7075 (a HAT-range art id on a torso slot, so getMCSComponent falls back to torso0). It is also the single 7xxx id inside the 153 'type-absent torso items' claim #32 counts. Around 90 further rows are stubs carrying only <id> plus at most <type> or <unique>. Measured over all 982 items: 804 carry <name> and 178 DO NOT (103 of the nameless are unique=2 NPC-wardrobe art, 75 are not) — those 178 render with an empty name.
new_findings.lane_impact: L-items-equipment: any item pipeline must survive a row with no fields at all and 178 nameless items, and a 1:1 recreation has to decide whether to reproduce the empty row or deviate — the same call claim #27 asks for on the other two bugs.

new_findings.text: The consumable modifier dispatch has a three-way numeric fallback that no claim decodes, plus nine named engine actions the packet's 'consumable effect table' omits. After the named branches, InventoryUI.onUseItem falls through to: modid < 2000 -> changeStat(modid, value) (so ANY id under 2000 is a stat delta, not just the 0-16 enum); modid >= 30000 -> setStat(modid, value) (a raw stat write); otherwise -> changeItemQty(modid, value), i.e. 'give `value` of item #modid'. itemdata exercises the second branch: item 2210 'Reset Quests' carries <modifier><id>40000</id>. Undocumented named branches: 34 (addGeneratedItemToInventory), 96 (teleport to territory dojo), 104/105/106 (loot-dialog control, RNG seed from server date, addLootItemBasic), 117 (wipe quest log + teleport), 123/124 (create clan).

new_findings.text: Positive mechanism evidence for why the v0.717 affix wording is gone, upgrading claim #34 from an absence argument. new_findings.text: The in-combat stance-change gate uses a different threshold in each build. Android v0.682 gates nextStance() on reload >= maxreload/6, which with the flat maxreload of 120 is 20 units = one sixth of the bar. The web v0.717 build gates the same action on Focus >= 48 against a max of 192 = one quarter of the bar. Anyone porting the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' threshold must take the web number and must not read the Android fraction as authoritative.
new_findings.quote: MCSPlayer.as:2977 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6) { return; }' with MCSPlayer.as:239 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' -> threshold 20/120 = 1/6. Web: §1t99s0§.as:249 '= 8 * 24' (192) with the documented Focus >= 48 gate -> 48/192 = 1/4.
new_findings.build: both — 1/6 on android v0.682, 1/4 on web v0.717
new_findings.lane_impact: L-combat-core / L-ui-hud: pins the stance-switch gate to a quarter bar for the v0.717 target and flags the Android bundle as an unsafe source for this specific constant.

new_findings.text: The reload/focus bar MAXIMUM is a hard-coded constant, not a SPEED formula, and it DIVERGES between builds: 5*24 = 120 on Android v0.682 and 8*24 = 192 on web v0.717. In both builds the value StatsManager.getBaseReload() computes (48 + SPEED*6) is passed into initPlayer, stored in a field, and never read by anything - it is dead code. This is a third android-vs-web tuning divergence beyond the two in itemdata/android-vs-web-constants-diverge, and it is what refutes itemdata/slashusage-is-a-reload-economy's bar-max half.
new_findings.quote: MCSPlayer.as:239 — 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' set INSIDE initPlayer, after :190 'this.baseReload = baseReload;'. MCSPlayer.as:105 — 'internal var baseReload:int = 48;'. StatsManager.as:1839-1842 — 'internal static function getBaseReload() : int { return 48 + (getPlayerStats(STAT_SPEED) + findBonusStat(STAT_SPEED)) * 6; }'. Web: §1t99s0§.as:249 — 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' and §1t99s0§.as:103 — 'internal var §1t4419s0§:int = 48;'. grep -rn "baseReload" reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ returns MCSPlayer.as:105,:182,:190 and EnemyClone.as:49 — declaration, parameter, assignment, copy. Zero readers. grep -rn "§1t4419s0§" reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/ returns §1t99s0§.as:103,:191 and §1t4904s0§.as:49. Zero readers.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1/L5 COMBAT CORE: the slash economy must be modelled as a flat 192-frame (8 s at 24 fps) bar for v0.717 fidelity, NOT as 48 + SPEED*6. SPEED does not lengthen the bar at all; it only affects reach and cooldowns. L6/L3: one more constant that must name its build. Also a general methodology lesson — a value that is computed and passed is not thereby used.
new_findings.ledger_text: itemdata/slashusage-is-a-reload-economy: 'the bar's max is 48 + SPEED*6, its floor is 24'

new_findings.text: The nine stat-bearing equipment slots are completely named in AS3 and match the nine paperdoll boxes box-for-box: {0 EQ_ARMOR, 1 EQ_GLOVES, 3 EQ_HAT, 5 EQ_MASK, 7 EQ_PANTS, 8 EQ_SHOES, 9 EQ_WEAPON, 11 EQ_ACCESSORY1, 12 EQ_ACCESSORY2}. The four body-only indices findBonusStat skips are 4 EQ_HEAD, 6 EQ_NECK, 10 EQ_SCABBARD, 2 EQ_HAIR. Nothing has to be invented for the two ring boxes.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/StatsManager.as:262-286 (EQ_* enum, 13 entries) and :1943-1945 (findBonusStat skip list); corroborated visually at reference/frames/s21_weapon/t708.0.png, crop (170,240)-(870,1045)
new_findings.quote: StatsManager.as:284 — 'internal static var EQ_ACCESSORY1:int = 11;'  ·  :286 — 'internal static var EQ_ACCESSORY2:int = 12;'  ·  :1943-1945 — 'for(var q:* = 0; q < 13; q++) { if(q != EQ_HEAD && q != EQ_NECK && q != EQ_SCABBARD && q != EQ_HAIR && !(skipWeapon && q == EQ_WEAPON))'. In the t708.0 crop the nine boxes are, in reading order: hat (straw hat, filled) / mask (ghost outline); armor (grey robe, filled) / gloves (ghost); pants (white hakama, filled) / weapon (pickaxe, filled); ring (ghost) / shoes (sandals, filled) / ring (ghost).
new_findings.lane_impact: L3 art-anim and L8 UI: the inventory screen's slot indices are contract, not inference — corrects itemdata/paperdoll-9-boxes-13-indices, which asserted the enum does not cover the two ring boxes.
new_findings.ledger_text: itemdata/paperdoll-9-boxes-13-indices: 'two of the nine boxes are ring/accessory slots that the named AS3 enum does not cover'

new_findings.text: Exactly two premium items carry a <heavenlyprice> but NO <baseprice> tag, so XMLItem's default fires and they are purchasable for 1 coin: item 2212 (heavenlyprice 5) and item 7049 (heavenlyprice 3). Every other Gold item writes <baseprice>0</baseprice>. This is the counterexample to 'Gold-only, not buyable with coins'.
new_findings.quote: itemdata.xml:2446-2454 — '<id>2212</id><type>10</type><name>4400</name><unique>1</unique><heavenlyprice>5</heavenlyprice><weight>0</weight><nogive>1</nogive><nodrop>1</nodrop><desc>4401</desc>' — no <baseprice> line at all. itemdata.xml:5218-5225 — '<id>7049</id><type>3</type><name>4346</name><unique>1</unique><heavenlyprice>3</heavenlyprice><defense>2</defense><weight>1</weight><desc>4347</desc>' — likewise. XMLItem.as:86-93 — 'if(xml.baseprice.toString() != "") { this.gvalue = xml.baseprice; } else { this.gvalue = 1; }'.
new_findings.lane_impact: L6 economy: the premium catalogue is 301 Gold-only rows plus 2 that also carry a 1-coin price. A recreation that hard-codes 'heavenlyprice > 0 implies coin price 0' will diverge on these two rows.
new_findings.ledger_text: itemdata/gold-catalogue: 'Every one of these rows also carries <baseprice>0</baseprice> — Gold-only, not buyable with coins.'

new_findings.text: ShopUI's sellPercentage = 0.5 has zero readers anywhere in the Android tree. Sell price is getSellAmt() alone; a recreation must not multiply by 0.5 on top of it.
new_findings.cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ShopUI.as:58; exhaustive grep -rn "sellPercentage" reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/ returns that one line
new_findings.quote: ShopUI.as:58 — 'internal var sellPercentage:Number = 0.5;'  — sole occurrence in the tree. The actual price is Item.as:1582-1593 getSellAmt(): 'if(this.itemID < 3000) { return 1; } if(this.getWeight() >= 10) { return (1 + this.getModifierCount()) * 10; } return (1 + this.getModifierCount()) * 5;'
new_findings.lane_impact: L6 economy: itemdata/sell-price-formula cites sellPercentage alongside the real formula; flagging it as dead prevents a 2x error in the sell path. Same dead-constant pattern as MCSPlayer.baseReload — this bundle carries several computed-then-discarded values, so every constant a lane adopts should be grep-checked for readers.
new_findings.ledger_text: itemdata/sell-price-formula cite includes 'ShopUI.as:58 — internal var sellPercentage:Number = 0.5'

new_findings.text: The <baseprice>. bug on item 11037 'Santa Pants' has no observable consequence: the item also carries <heavenlyprice>3</heavenlyprice>, and every other Gold-priced row in the file writes <baseprice>0</baseprice>, so int('.') = 0 produces exactly the value the row was meant to have. There is no 'reproduce or deviate' decision with a stake in it.
new_findings.quote: itemdata.xml:6898-6905 — '<id>11037</id><type>7</type><name>4204</name><unique>1</unique><baseprice>.</baseprice><heavenlyprice>3</heavenlyprice><defense>1</defense><weight>5</weight>'. Measured over all 982 items: 303 rows carry a non-zero <heavenlyprice>; 300 of them write <baseprice>0</baseprice>. 11037 is the only one that writes '.'.
new_findings.lane_impact: L6 economy: itemdata/baseprice-dot-data-bug is factually correct but its 'a 1:1 recreation has to decide' framing overstates the stake — the bug is inert. Worth carrying so the lane does not spend a decision cycle on it.
new_findings.ledger_text: itemdata/baseprice-dot-data-bug: 'a 1:1 recreation has to decide to reproduce or deviate, not silently fix'

The 24 Hz conclusion is right and I verified it myself (web SWF header: CWS v17, rect [0,16000,0,13800], framerate 24.0). But the claim's TEXT asserts it is 'corroborated by the trap duty cycles', and that corroboration is FALSE. I parsed every <property> in 93_1t4647s0.bin against the file's own schema comment: 75 duty-cycle values are NOT multiples of 24. The surveyor quoted one of its own counter-examples — line 451 `<property>0,24,36,0,1,1,1</property>` is Trap_SpikesAuto (direction,onDuration,offDuration,...), so offDuration=36. Measured domain: startInterval {0,6,8,12,16,18,24,30,32,36,42,48,54,64,72}, offDuration {0,24,36,48,60,96,1000}, onDuration {0,24,48}; gcd = 2, not 24. A false universal in the claim text must not enter the ledger. See new finding bindata/duty-cycle-domain-measured for the corrected version, which preserves the 24 Hz result.

I decoded the GIF myself and printed all 72 rows. The claim TEXT is true and I verified every link myself: web SWF header CWS v17, rect [0,16000,0,13800], framerate 24.0; GameEngine.as:442 `stageMC.addEventListener(Event.ENTER_FRAME,gameloop);`; MCSCharacter.as:1315-1319 `++this.frameCounter; if(this.frameCounter < this.currentAnimationDuration) { this.updateFrame(); }` — one authored keyframe per stage tick. REFUTED — the two scales are fully reconcilable and the transform is entirely in the payload. WorldMapUI.as:15/17/19 (== WarSelectUI.as:15/17/19): WARMARKERSHIFTX=8, TERRSHIFTX=21, TERRSHIFTY=51, and the 12-bit fields are BIASED BY 341. Forward, QuestEngine.as:522-526: `if(mapBitmapData.getPixel(i,j) != 0) { terrX = i - TERRSHIFTX + WARMARKERSHIFTX; terrY = j - TERRSHIFTY; warMarkerList.push(terrX + 341 << 12 | terrY + 341); }`. Inverse, QuestEngine.as:1206: `getPixel(x + TERRSHIFTX - 341 - WARMARKERSHIFTX, y + TERRSHIFTY - 341)`. Collapsed: pixel_x = rawTerrX - 328, pixel_y = rawTerrY - 290. I tested it against the decoded GIF: Ibamaya 1405272 -> pixel (15,54) LAND; Gokura 1524045 -> (44,43) LAND; web-only Iwakuni 1519945 -> (43,39) LAND. All three hardcoded towns land on land. The claim's own guess ('both land near territory (57,57)') is also wrong — the biased pairs are (2,3) and (31,-8). Web parity confirmed at §1t7934s0§.as:15,17,19 = 8,21,51 and §1t1524s0§.as:1463.

Web build agrees: §1t1524s0§.as:1283 and §1t7785s0§.as:1525. These are rival PLAYERS, not missing NPC rows. Claim bindata/war-boss-ids-are-rival-players already carries the correct reading; this one must not be banked beside it.

REFUTED at the load-bearing level. The arithmetic is right (98:676 is 'Uenohara', table has 677 entries, getTownName1 index = namex*26+namey, namestarting=78 / nameending=37 confirmed by counting the arrays, and the two hardcoded towns at :137-144 are real). But the 26x26 branch is UNREACHABLE. NameGenerator.as:147-149 gates it on `namex = territoryx % 137` being < 26, and I derived the real domain of territoryx from QuestEngine.as:522-526 plus the decoded 63x72 bitmap: every one of the 735 land territories has raw x in [329,389], so namex is in [55,115] — always >= 26. getTownName1 is called for ZERO real territories; every shipped place name is a hardcoded exception or a getTownName2 compound. bindata/98's 677 names are dormant data in the world map, not 'the world-naming algorithm recovered whole'. REFUTED — this is a search failure, not a missing artifact, and it is the single most valuable recovery in the packet. MCSPlayer.setStance (MCSPlayer.as:3019-3095) sets the reach cap per stance: LIGHT = baseSlashLength*1.5 (:3030); BALANCED = baseSlashLength*(1 + 0.5*balancedMastery*0.01) (:3041); HEAVY = baseSlashLength*(0.5 + 0.5*heavyMastery*0.01) with a floor of 100 (:3052-3055); REVERSED = *1.5 (:3067); DUAL = base with floor 100 (:3078-3081); then `InputManager.setMaxDistance(this.slashLength)` (:3094). The base is StatsManager.as:1915-1918 `getBaseSlashLengthVal(speed) = int(120 + Math.floor((90 + STAT_DAN*5) * speed / (20 + speed)))`, speed = STAT_SPEED + bonus, x1.5 under BUFF_SPEED (:1907-1911); BUFF_INJURED halves it (MCSPlayer.as:222); AI uses maxincrement 90 fixed (EnemyPlayer.as:757). InputManager.as:51 default maxDistance = 200. It is in STAGE PIXELS and it is web-verified (§1t1523s0§.as:2347). The surveyor's grep missed it because the class is MCSPlayer.as (not Player.as) and the symbol is slashLength/baseSlashLength.

new_findings.text: THE PER-STANCE REACH CAP IN STAGE PIXELS IS RECOVERED IN FULL. MCSPlayer.setStance sets it per stance and feeds it straight to the input line: LIGHT = baseSlashLength*1.5; BALANCED = baseSlashLength*(1 + 0.5*balancedMastery*0.01); HEAVY = baseSlashLength*(0.5 + 0.5*heavyMastery*0.01) with a hard floor of 100; REVERSED = *1.5; DUAL = base with floor 100; then InputManager.setMaxDistance(slashLength). The base is 120 + floor((90 + STAT_DAN*5) * speed / (20 + speed)), speed = STAT_SPEED + bonus, x1.5 under BUFF_SPEED, halved by BUFF_INJURED. AI opponents use the same shape with maxincrement fixed at 90. Default before any stance is set is 200. So reach IS the stance trade-off: light reaches 1.5x, heavy only 0.5x at zero mastery and reaches parity only at 100% heavy mastery.

new_findings.text: The trap system ships with a debug override the packet never mentions, and it is the source of the census inflation in bindata/trap-census-and-800-is-one-screen. RoomGenNode checks for a <default> element in traproomdata BEFORE any tier selection and, if present, replaces every trap room in the game with it. 93_1t4647s0.bin:22-30 is exactly that block, shipped commented out — which is why raw greps of the file return 70 rooms and 314 objects instead of the live 69 and 297.

new_findings.text: Trap-room placement has FIVE paths, not the three in bindata/trap-room-placement-and-level-gate. A fourth converts key rooms into ROOM_TRAPKEY, and a fifth places the veryhard tier as a dedicated 6-room route — which is exactly why veryhard alone gets the daily reroll.

new_findings.text: The exact hues of the drawn slash line — the most visible element of a duel — are two constants in the input layer, identical in both builds. The player's guide line is drawn green when the slash is affordable and dark red otherwise, and the stroke tapers as the allowed distance is consumed; the enemy's line is drawn pure black.
new_findings.quote: InputManager.as:172-180 `public static function greenLine() : * { canvas.graphics.lineStyle(thickness,39168,1,…); }` / `public static function redLine() : * { canvas.graphics.lineStyle(thickness,10027008,1,…); }` — 39168 = 0x009900, 10027008 = 0x990000. :360 `lineStyle(thickness - thickness * ((maxDistance - distanceLeft) / maxDistance),10027008,…)` — the taper. :492 the enemy line uses colour `0`. WEB §1t1541s0§.as:174,179,361 identical.

new_findings.text: The engine's own letterbox/pillarbox algorithm, which resolves the apparent 800x690-vs-800x480 contradiction between the web SWF header and the longplay frames. The base canvas is 800x480; 690 is 800x480 plus a 210px friend bar that is only shown when the window is TALLER than 800/690. The engine fits width or height, centres with an offset, and publishes stageScale / stageOffsetX / stageOffsetY / stageFitWidth / stageBaseWidth / stageBaseHeight — the same values InputManager uses to convert mouse coordinates back into stage space.
new_findings.quote: GameEngine.as:269-274 `var originalWidth:int = 800; var originalHeight:int = 480; var originalHeightWithBar:int = 690; var originalAspectRatio:Number = originalWidth / originalHeight; var originalWithBarAspectRatio:Number = originalWidth / originalHeightWithBar; var newAspectRatio:Number = stageMC.stageWidth / stageMC.stageHeight;` ; :293-306 fit-width vs fit-height with `offsetX = (stageMC.stageWidth - originalWidth * newScale) / 2;` ; :307-312 publishes stageScale/stageOffsetX/stageOffsetY/stageFitWidth/stageBaseWidth/stageBaseHeight ; InputManager.as:185-186 `mouseX = (args.stageX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale;`
new_findings.lane_impact: L-render/L-input: the frame still wins on what the playfield is (1816x1080 measured, 5:3), and this is the code that produces those pillars. It also gives the exact screen-to-stage mapping any input port needs.

new_findings.text: The web v0.717 Focus bar's hidden dead zone is 48, not the 24 the packet reports from the Android build. Displayed fill = (reload - 48) / (192 - 48), so the bar reads exactly zero precisely while reload <= 48, which is exactly when the stance change is refused: the bar and the CANNOT CHANGE STANCE gate are the same predicate. This is also the constant that makes the longplay measurement come out right — 44.7 px/s predicted vs 42.5 px/s measured, against 38.3 px/s from the Android-24 model.

new_findings.text: The +6 Focus reward fires on a KILL, not on a landed slash. Both builds gate bonusReload() behind a count of enemies that just died this resolution pass. This inverts the meter economy the packet describes: connecting gives nothing back, so a long single-target duel drains Focus monotonically until the enemy dies.

new_findings.text: The Focus meter is emptied at slash RELEASE, before any hit test runs, in both builds. deductReloadBar() zeroes a full bar then subtracts the per-stance slashUsage, and it is called from endSlash() ahead of NPCManager.checkHit(). Damage (including the crit multiply) is frozen even earlier, at slash launch. A whiffed crit therefore costs the entire meter.
new_findings.lane_impact: L-combat-core feel: the crit is a committed swing, not a rewarded hit. A recreation that refunds a missed crit plays measurably differently.

new_findings.build: android v0.682; the same pages render in web v0.717 (verified verbatim on frames 1/7, 3/7, 6/7)
new_findings.cite: strings.json["376"], ["372"], ["378"], ["380"]; rendering verified at reference/frames/Nr4fQstqHDM/seg-20/frames/frame_0011.jpg, frame_0012.jpg, frame_0013.jpg
new_findings.quote:
["376"] '- Troops will advance on enemy sectors every 24 hours.

- If a sector has more attacking troops than defending troops, the sector will be captured by the attackers.

- The Clan that captures all the control points in the battlefield will gain control of the territory.' ["372"] '- the effect of moves is dependent on the terrain. mountains have the highest tactical advantage, followed by forests and fields.

- the clan will pay the player 5 coins per move made.' ["380"] names Command HQ / Forward base / Barricades / Tunnels / Towns at 500 coins per contributing player.
new_findings.ledger_text: (3) real-world "day" length (governs expiry, farming, AP regen, war tick).
new_findings.lane_impact: meta-social, world-exploration, economy: the war-tick half of blocker (3) closes outright

new_findings.text: The gold-to-resource exchange rate is stated twice and identically: 1 Gold buys 10 AP or 10 Duel Tokens. Token IAP packs and a max-token cap exist too. Separately, the frame that shows the stable price shows NO AP component, so the ledger's 'stable 14c+5AP' needs its own cite for the +5AP half or should be trimmed.
new_findings.build: android v0.682 strings; stable price from web v0.717 frame

["4173"]/["4174"]/["4175"] '10 Duel Tokens'/'25 Duel Tokens'/'40 Duel Tokens'. frame_0048: 'STABLEHAND / WOULD YOU LIKE TO RENT A HORSE TO TRAVEL TO A NEIGHBOURING VILLAGE? / COST: 14 COINS' - no AP line rendered.
new_findings.ledger_text: **Economy statics:** ... stable 14c+5AP ...
new_findings.lane_impact: economy: adds the hard-currency conversion rate; puts the '+5AP' half of the stable static in doubt

new_findings.text: The 30-minute buff timer governs a six-member family, not the single damage buff the packet found: four 150% buffs and two 200% regeneration buffs, each carrying the same one-buff-at-a-time clause.
new_findings.build: android v0.682; the Damage member verified rendering verbatim on a web v0.717 frame
new_findings.quote: ["4132"] 150% Damage, ["4133"] 150% Defense, ["4134"] 150% XP, ["4135"] 150% Speed, ["4229"] 200% AP Regeneration, ["4230"] 200% Duel Token Regeneration - all ending 'Note: Only one buff may be active at a time.'
new_findings.lane_impact: items-equipment, economy, ui-hud: the buff HUD widget must render six labels, not one

new_findings.text: Two corrections to the clan set. First, the fourth (green-fist) crest resolves: Clan Midori Ken - the four clan names are closed at Aka Ryu, Midori Ken, Aoi Hoiru, Ki Sensu. Second, the game contradicts itself on domains: two different clan cards both claim the NORTH-EAST, so a rebuild that mirrors a clean four-point compass will diverge from the OG.
new_findings.build: web v0.717 frames; names from android v0.682
new_findings.cite: reference/frames/Nr4fQstqHDM/seg-20/frames/frame_0007.jpg and frame_0001.jpg (both read whole @1.9x); names at strings.json["289"]-["292"]; bios at strings.json["326"], ["327"]
new_findings.quote: frame_0007: 'CLAN KI SENSU RULES THE DOMAIN IN THE NORTH-EAST.' frame_0001: 'CLAN AKA RYU RULES THE DOMAIN IN THE NORTH-EAST.' Same compass point, two clans. Names: ["289"] 'Aka Ryu Crops', ["290"] 'Midori Ken Crops', ["291"] 'Aoi Hoiru Crops', ["292"] 'Ki Sensu Crops' (Midori = green, Ken = fist -> the green-fist crest).
new_findings.lane_impact: meta-social: completes the crest-to-name binding for all four clans and logs an OG defect so a rebuild does not 'fix' it silently

new_findings.text: The death card header DOES resolve to the string table even though its two buttons do not, and there is a separate war-room death string nobody has surfaced. Small but it tightens claim 6: the card is a mix of table-backed and hardcoded copy.

new_findings.quote: Frame header 'YOU WERE DEFEATED!' == strings.json["92"] 'You were defeated!' exactly. strings.json["831"] = 'You were defeated in the war room!' - a second, war-room-specific defeat path that never appears in any ledger system.
